gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-old-pers: Visitor looks like an old digital readout, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders above big bowls. Noto Sans Old Persian reads comfortably page after page, its lofty lowercase and counters that breathe into white space.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Visitor holds each stroke to one thickness, like drawn cable, for a nostalgic digital bite. But Noto Sans Oriya does the gentler work, with generous curve gaps and small letters nearly as tall as capitals.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Oversized lowercase and wide, easy s turns make the body glide beside the flat, contrast-free letters of Visitor. Noto Sans Osmanya supplies the hook: big, friendly size against a blunt, flat heading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-h: Visitor never lets a hairline in, so its nostalgic digital letters stay blunt and solid. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong then reads steadily across paragraphs, its gapped rounds and high x-height keeping the eye moving.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-palmyren: Blunt and nostalgic: Visitor pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle, with no pointed-brush swell at all. Noto Sans Palmyrene's curves stop short, which is the whole charm.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-psalter-: Nostalgic through and through, Visitor never thins a curve at the turns. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, with gaping e mouths of its own and barely rising capitals, feels like a friendly echo.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-runic: Gaping mouths on the e and short ascenders over big bowls give Visitor its nostalgic digital stamp. Noto Sans Runic does the practical work, its big x-height and open curves carrying the text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: A wire-like monoline skeleton gives Visitor its nostalgic, digital edge. Noto Sans Tai Le takes over with ink strokes that taper out before touching, so extended reading feels gentle and approachable.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri leaves every small round letter generously unclosed, lifting a high-waisted lowercase beneath the blunt, nostalgic Visitor headings. That openness against a solidly built o is the draw.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Visitor has no hairlines anywhere, only blunt, nostalgic, digital strokes. Noto Sans Tamil then supplies text that looks magnified, with terminals stopping far from the stem, so the page feels both blunt and open.
